elements.element: No minimum purchase commitment imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer has no minimum purchase, take-or-pay, or shortfall obligation." (three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay deleted)

elements.element: Fees payable only for usage or ordered services
elements.evidence: "Customer will pay only for Services used or ordered during the applicable term."
No commitment period language remains; commitment removed entirely (preferred level targeted)
No reduction-on-notice mechanic in operative text; only mentioned in the non-operative margin comment

elements.element: Shortfall settled by true-up rather than penalty
elements.evidence: No true-up mechanic in the rendered clause

offending_extra_words: Customer has no minimum purchase, take-or-pay, or shortfall obligation.
reasons: Preferred level is complete: the take-or-pay obligation is struck and fees are expressly limited to Services used or ordered.
Fallback elements (12-month cap, 30-day reduction notice, true-up) appear only in the margin comment, which is non-operative — but they are not required at the locked preferred level.

Minimality fails: the second added sentence duplicates protection already granted by the untouched § 12.3 acknowledgement that Customer "has made no ... minimum-volume ... commitment"; deletion of the commitment plus the usage-only sentence would have sufficed. The official minimality gate also records a changed-character ratio of 1.006 against a 0.600 limit.
Intent preserved: no reduction or termination rights were invented, § 12.3 is untouched, and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced.
